title: Tensor and K-flat transport along a ring-sheaf isomorphism
statement:
Let $J$ be a site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $R,S$ be sheaves of commutative rings, and let $c:R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ be a ring-sheaf isomorphism. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheafified balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and restriction $C_c=\operatorname{Res}_c:\operatorname{Mod}(S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Then $C_c$ is an additive exact equivalence with inverse $C_{c^{-1}}$. It has coherent natural isomorphisms
$$C_c(M\otimes_S N)\cong C_cM\otimes_R C_cN,\qquad C_cS\cong R,$$
whose tensor map and inverse both send a local pure tensor to the same pure tensor, and whose unit map is $c^{-1}$. They respect associators, unitors and symmetry. Termwise $C_c$ identifies the direct-sum total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], preserves and reflects acyclicity, flat modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]. On either module category, the acyclic-tensor test for K-flatness is equivalent to requiring both total tensor functors to preserve quasi-isomorphisms [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. On unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its termwise extension therefore has a coherent natural comparison
$$D(C_c)(K\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}L)\cong D(C_c)K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D(C_c)L,$$
computed by the preceding total-complex map on corresponding K-flat resolutions.

source.place: Tag 06YP, lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism; ring-isomorphism specialization of the total-tensor and K-flat argument. Tensor convention supplied by def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product (sites-modules.tex, section-tensor-product). Agent-written scalar-coordinate comparison, with complete proof in report.md.

proof.text: Put $C=C_c$ and $B=C_{c^{-1}}$. By restriction of scalars, $r\in R(U)$ acts on $CM(U)$ as $c_U(r)$, while $s\in S(U)$ acts on $BF(U)$ as $c_U^{-1}(s)$. Consequently $BCM\cong M$ and $CBF\cong F$ by the identity on underlying abelian sheaves, naturally on all module morphisms. These identities obey the triangle identities. Both functors preserve addition of morphisms. They preserve limits and colimits by their universal properties: the natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_R(CM,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(M,BF)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(F,CM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(BF,M)$ identify cones and cocones and their unique factorizations. In particular both functors are exact and preserve all small direct sums. The site-size hypothesis ensures that the module categories are abelian.

source.place: Section 03CS, presheaves and sheaves of modules; scalar-coordinate argument for an invertible ring map

proof.text: For every $U$, define $t_U:C(M(U)\otimes_{S(U)}N(U))\to CM(U)\otimes_{R(U)}CN(U)$ by $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes n$. It is well-defined: for $s\in S(U)$ write $s=c_U(r)$, so $(sm)\otimes n=(rm)\otimes n=m\otimes(rn)=m\otimes(sn)$ in the target. The same formula in the reverse direction is $R(U)$-balanced because $r$ acts through $c_U(r)$. Both maps are $R(U)$-linear and inverse on generators. They commute with restriction maps since $c$ and $c^{-1}$ are maps of ring sheaves. Restriction commutes with module sheafification: for any presheaf $P$ of $S$-modules and $R$-module sheaf $F$, maps $CP\to F$ correspond to maps $P\to BF$, hence uniquely to maps $P^\#\to BF$ and then to maps $C(P^\#)\to F$. Thus $C(P^\#)\cong(CP)^\#$ by the sheafification universal property. Sheafifying $t_U$ and its inverse gives the asserted natural tensor isomorphism $t_{M,N}$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; explicit scalar-coordinate argument

proof.text: Define $e:CS\to R$ by $e_U(s)=c_U^{-1}(s)$. It is $R$-linear since $c_U^{-1}(c_U(r)s)=r c_U^{-1}(s)$, and its inverse is $c$. The sheaf tensor constraints are induced by the sectionwise module constraints. In the associator diagram both composites send $(m\otimes n)\otimes z$ to $m\otimes(n\otimes z)$. In the symmetry diagram both send $m\otimes n$ to $n\otimes m$. In the left-unit diagram the path through $t$ and $e$ sends $s\otimes m$ to $c_U^{-1}(s)\cdot_Rm=sm$, which is the image under the original $S$-unitor; the right-unit check is $m\otimes s\mapsto sm$. Equalities on pure tensors imply equality on presheaf tensors by linearity, and on their sheafifications by uniqueness. This proves coherence, including the specified unit normalization.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, associativity formulas; Tag 03EO, lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor

proof.text: Apply the exact-functor cohomology comparison to the exact additive functors $C,B$ of step 1. It gives $H^n(CK)\cong C(H^nK)$ and the analogous comparison for $B$, naturally in chain maps. Since $BC\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $CB\cong\mathrm{id}$, each functor preserves and reflects zero objects and isomorphisms. Thus each termwise functor preserves and reflects acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms, with no boundedness condition.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, applied to kernels and images in each degree

proof.text:
Use preservation of direct sums from step 1 and $t$ from step 2 on every summand to define
$$t^n_{P,Q}:C\left(\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P^p\otimes_SQ^q\right)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{p+q=n}CP^p\otimes_RCQ^q.$$
On the $(p,q)$ summand it sends $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$. The differential on both sides sends this tensor to $d_Px\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes d_Qy$; additivity of $C$ preserves the sign. Hence $t_{P,Q}$ is a natural chain isomorphism. The total associator is the sum-reindexing map $(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$; the two bracketings have differential $d_P+(-1)^p d_Q+(-1)^{p+q}d_H$ on degree $(p,q,r)$. The total symmetry is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$: after differentiating its two terms have signs $(-1)^{pq}$ and $(-1)^{pq+q}$, the same as after applying symmetry to the differential. Thus these are chain maps and the scalar comparison commutes with them, with the unitors, and with their coherence diagrams by the summand checks of step 3. The identical construction works for $B$.

source.place: Tag 06YM, lemma-derived-tor-exact, total-tensor convention; signed summand calculation

proof.text: If $M$ is a flat $S$-module sheaf, let $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to0$ be any exact sequence of $R$-module sheaves. Apply the exact $B$, tensor with $M$, and apply the exact $C$. The result is exact; steps 1-2 identify its terms and maps with $F_i\otimes_R CM$. Thus $CM$ is flat. The same argument with $B$ proves the converse and proves preservation and reflection for both functors.

source.place: Tag 03ER, definition-flat, item (3); exactness and tensor comparison from steps 1-2

proof.text: Suppose $P$ is K-flat over $S$ and $F$ is any acyclic $R$-complex. Step 4 makes $BF$ acyclic, so $\operatorname{Tot}(BF\otimes_SP)$ is acyclic by K-flatness. Apply $C$ and steps 1 and 5 to identify its image with $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_RCP)$, which is acyclic by step 4. Thus $CP$ is K-flat. Interchanging $C,B$ proves preservation in the reverse direction; the natural identities $BC\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $CB\cong\mathrm{id}$ then prove reflection. This quantifies over all acyclic complexes, not just those originally presented over the other ring.

source.place: Tag 06YN, definition-K-flat; scalar transport using steps 1, 4 and 5

proof.text: Fix either ring sheaf $T=R$ or $S$. If $P$ satisfies the acyclic-tensor definition, signed symmetry from step 5 also makes $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_T A)$ acyclic for every acyclic $A$. For any quasi-isomorphism $f:X\to Y$, its cone is acyclic by the cone criterion. The tensor-cone isomorphism identifies $\operatorname{Cone}(1_P\otimes f)$ with $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_T\operatorname{Cone}(f))$, which is acyclic. The cone criterion makes $1_P\otimes f$ a quasi-isomorphism, and signed symmetry gives the same for $f\otimes1_P$. Conversely, if both total tensor functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms, apply $-\otimes_TP$ to $0\to A$ for every acyclic $A$. Its image has zero source, so its being a quasi-isomorphism means that $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_TP)$ is acyclic. This is exactly K-flatness in the acyclic-tensor definition, and proves its equivalence with the two-sided quasi-isomorphism convention.

source.place: Tag 06YP, lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism, proof via Tag 06YM and acyclic cones; converse using the zero map to an acyclic complex

proof.text: By step 4 the functor $Q_RC$ on complexes inverts all quasi-isomorphisms, so the localization universal property gives $D(C)$ with $D(C)Q_S\cong Q_RC$. Likewise it gives $D(B)$. The natural identities from step 1 descend, by full faithfulness of precomposition with localization, to $D(B)D(C)\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $D(C)D(B)\cong\mathrm{id}$. These specify the induced exact equivalence on unbounded derived categories. On homotopies termwise $C$ preserves $f-g=dh+hd$ by additivity, so these comparisons can equally be computed in the homotopy categories used below. Termwise $C$ commutes with shifts and sends the cone differential matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_Y&f\\0&-d_X\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ to the same matrix for $Cf$, using preservation of finite sums and negatives. Thus the descended equivalence preserves the distinguished cone triangles.

source.place: Tags 04VG and 04VK, localization universal properties; natural-transformation version stated in the cited node

proof.text:
Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $P\to K$ and $Q\to L$ over $S$, which exist for arbitrary unbounded complexes. By steps 4, 6 and 7 their $C$-images are flat-term K-flat resolutions of $CK,CL$. On such pairs use the canonical total-tensor models of derived tensor and define the comparison as
$$D(C)(Q_SP\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Q_SQ)\cong Q_RC\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_SQ)\xrightarrow{Q_R(t_{P,Q})}Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(CP\otimes_RCQ)\cong D(C)Q_SP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D(C)Q_SQ.$$
The maps are natural in both homotopy-category variables by step 5 and the model isomorphisms. The resolving-subcategory descent theorem extends this natural isomorphism uniquely to all derived pairs. Its inverse extends the inverse of $t$. In particular it is independent of the chosen resolutions and is computed by the preceding total-complex map on corresponding resolutions.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; definition-derived-tor and preceding localization construction following Tag 06YT

proof.text: The regular module $T$ is flat because $-\otimes_TT\cong\mathrm{id}$, and $T[0]$ is K-flat because $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_TT[0])\cong A$. The derived associator, unitors and symmetry of $D(T)$ are those of the derived symmetric monoidal structure, induced on total tensor complexes of K-flat representatives by the module constraints and by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$; on flat-term K-flat $P,Q$ its tensor is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_TQ)$, the same model as in the tensor-descent theorem. Therefore the derived unit comparison is represented by $e:CS\to R$. For three flat-term K-flat complexes, their pairwise total tensors are again flat-term K-flat by the total-tensor model lemma. Hence the derived associator diagram is represented by the chain associator diagram of step 5; it commutes on every triple summand. The derived symmetry and unit diagrams are represented by the signed symmetry and scalar-action checks in steps 3 and 5. To obtain equality on arbitrary derived objects, use faithfulness of restriction to flat-term K-flat models from the tensor-descent theorem, for diagrams in three variables first in two variables with the third fixed at a model, then in the remaining variable (the same statement applied to bifunctors constant in one variable). This proves the claimed coherent natural comparison.
